_about: Best current values for a part-level 3D/2D model of a single-lift, single-cylinder Jacquard head on a treadle hand loom, compiled from ../sources/notes-mechanism.md. Values are given in inches (the unit of the 1878-1912 sources) and millimetres (in x 25.4, rounded to 0.1 mm). basis: doc = stated as a number in a document or museum record; drawing = scaled from a dimensioned or to-scale drawing; photo = scaled from a photo; derived = computed from doc values (the computation is in 'note'); est = estimate. confidence: high = documented and corroborated; medium = one good source or a consistent derivation; low = estimate or a source for a different machine. Source keys are defined in the Sources list at the end of ../sources/notes-mechanism.md. Posselt's dimensioned machine (Figs I-XI, pp. 11-17, drawn 1/4 full size) is a 200-hook (208-needle) cast-iron single-lift machine; it is used as the reference head because it is the only fully dimensioned one found.

machine.value: Single-lift single-cylinder Jacquard head, 200-hook class (208 needles and hooks = 26 x 8, 8 knives), closed (bottom-closed) shed, swing-batten card cylinder driven from the griffe by an S-iron / swan neck, griffe lifted by a treadle and cord through a head lever; on a four-post treadle hand loom with throw or fly shuttle and hand-wound take-up.
machine.note: Bradbury p. 68: the single lift is 'the only type of machine adopted for figure weaving in the hand ... looms'. Posselt p. 12 describes a hand-loom lift from above (strap on a wooden drum); Bradbury Fig. 65 and Barlow p. 157 a head lever with a cord to the treadle. Model the head lever version (one rotating lever, one cord).
alternatives: 400-hook head (8 x 50 + 2 reserve rows = 416 needles: NELSON1909; 408 = 8 x 51: BRADBURY1912) - same parts, longer knives and cylinder
Double-lift single-cylinder (two griffes, two hooks per needle, semi-open shed: POSSELT1888 pp. 67-69) - not for a first model
Double-lift double-cylinder (two complete selecting sets: POSSELT1888 p. 69; NELSON1909) - not for a first model

hook_layouts._note: N-hook machine = N needles = N hooks; rows = hooks per cross-row = knives = needles per vertical tier.

sizes_in_common_use.note: Posselt p. 9; size excludes the (generally two) reserve rows

alternatives: 28 cross-rows x 8 = 224 of which 25 cross-rows (200) used, first and last two reserved (BRADBURY1912 p. 70, Fig. 65)
h200.note: Posselt Fig. XIV card: 26 x 8 = 208 holes; Fig. VII: 208 needles; Fig. 22 (appendix): 26th row is the reserve row

h400.note: Nelson: needle board for a 400 machine has 416 holes in 52 rows of 8, split by a lacing groove into 26 + 26 rows; so '26 x 16' is two halves of 26 x 8, not a 16-row machine. Posselt Fig. XXIX: neck cords 1-8 in the first row, 393-400 in the 50th.

h900_h1200_french_index.note: Posselt p. 88: piano-machine rack pins (one per card row position). Row count (12 or 16) not stated; 12-row is an inference.

french_fine_16_row.note: Bell (1895) Fig. 31: French machines with 16 rows 'much closer set'; McMurdo's 1296-hook machine also 16-row (1296 = 16 x 81)

verdol_896.note: Each 8-hole row is two staggered lines (patent: lines 3a/3b offset), cf. Bell: 'two rows of 8 making one row of 16 hooks'. 1344 = 3 x 448 is an inference, not found stated.

material.value: cast iron (US); wood for European hand-loom machines

main_width.note: Fig. I, 6 to 7; front-to-back size of the 200 machine frame side

height_parts.note: bottom casting, lower opening, middle casting, upper opening, top casting

plunger_diameter.note: griffe guide rod; slides in 3 shouldered bearings (frame heights 2 3/4, 2, 2 in at k, l, m)

size.note: length x width x thickness; one hole per hook; screwed to the frame

hole_pitch_along_knife.note: 'a, in length of board' - i.e. between cross-rows (26 per board)

hole_pitch_across_knives.note: 'b, in width' - equals the griffe-bar pitch

knife_count.note: one knife per hook row; 12 for a 12-row machine

knife_section.value: strong hoop iron with feather (bevelled) edges, set inclined
knife_section.note: Barlow p. 150, p. 157: the inclined face of a descending bar strikes the face of an unpushed hook and forces it back until the bar is below the crook

alternatives: about 4 in (cradle lever 28:10, NELSON1909; BRADBURY1912 problems pp. 301-302)
3 1/2 in harness draw in Bell's example (BELL1895)
'If the griffe is raised two inches' (BELL1895, a rise-and-fall machine)
lift_stroke.note: Nelson: overhead lever 10 1/2 in : 25 in, 8 in crank stroke -> 10.5 x 8 / 25 = 3 1/3 in, 'about a three-inch shed'. Use 3 1/2 in (88.9 mm) as default.

rester_height.note: turned-up lower leg, b to c

crook.value: top bent over toward the knife (towards the needle board in double-lift machines)

bottom.value: doubled wire turned up about 1/3 of its length through a fixed grate; double loop rests in the tug (bottom) board
alternatives: lower bend fits a wooden grate suspended from the griffe that rises with it (BARLOW1878 p. 152)

loop_length.note: rear loop; spring sits on it; pin through it limits forward travel

head_to_eye_example.note: varies by row: 8 positions in an 8-row machine; top needle's eye nearest the needle board (NELSON1909)

eye_position_rule.value: eye_n at the hook of row n: needle 1 (top) serves the hook nearest the needle board, needle 8 (bottom) the hook nearest the spring box

alternatives: about 1/4 in (BARLOW1878 p. 150, checked on page image)
protrusion_from_board.note: this is also the needle stroke when a blank presses it flush

vertical_pitch.note: 'The needles are placed at about 1/4 in. apart' (p. 157, checked on page image)

horizontal_pitch.note: assumed = cross-row pitch of the hooks (needles run straight back to their hooks)

housing.value: spring box (wood, one hole per needle, one pin per vertical needle row) or spring on the needle loop held by a pin through the loop

size.note: not found; model 4-5 mm OD x 25 mm
Fig. XI, a to c and a to b (front view)

peg_holes.note: receive the cylinder pegs (about 1/2 in long)

material.value: wood preferred (wears needles less) or metal; lace grooves at ends and centre (400 machine)

shape.value: square prism, hard well-seasoned wood with iron ends, holes bored in each face to match the needles

face_width.note: 'height of cylinder' 2 7/16 in = side of the square

lantern_size.note: square end piece with rounded corners (Bradbury, Nelson) or four pins (Barlow p. 153)

pegs_per_face.note: one near each end; brass; adjustable sideways

travel_out.note: 'The cylinder is moved out from the needle board from two to three inches' (power, swing batten)

clearance_when_turning_starts.note: cylinder about 1/4 in from the needle points when it begins to turn

type.value: square iron frame hung on two pointed centre screws at the top of the machine; cylinder in brass cups with height-adjusting screws

drive.value: bowl on the griffe running in an S-iron / swan neck fixed to the frame (hand loom)

swing_radius.note: not found; make the pivot-to-cylinder-axis about 16-18 in so a 2.5 in travel is about 8-9 deg

function.value: spring-loaded presser on the lantern square from below (Posselt Fig. X) or from above (Bradbury Fig. 66, Barlow p. 154); steadies the cylinder and squares it

count.value: 2 (top catch turns forward, bottom catch turns back) + optional protecting catch

reverse_control.value: cord within the weaver's reach lifts the top catch and engages the bottom catch

card_springs.value: flat springs on the batten pressing the cards to the cylinder

head_lever.value: simple lever on a post above the machine, link to the griffe, cord from the outer end to the treadle

head_lever_arms_power.note: 36 in overhead lever for a power loom: 10 1/2 in griffe arm, 24-25 2/3 in rod arm; no hand-loom figure found

posselt_strap_drum_diameter.note: hand-loom alternative: wooden drum on a shaft, leather strap to the plunger, triangular frame 14 1/4 in high

treadle.value: 'simple tread lever of the second order adjusted near the weaver's foot'

counterpoise.value: weights or springs when the load is heavy; single-acting head otherwise rests with griffe down

material.value: strong pasteboard, laced into an endless chain

card_200_french_index.note: lacing frame data p. 97: card length 9 5/8 in, width 2 5/16 in, peg centres 7 1/2 in apart, peg dia 3/8 in at the bottom, 1/4 in between cards on the frame

card_408_ordinary_english.note: 'each pattern card measures 16 1/2 x 2 1/2 in = 41.25 sq ins' (p. 245, checked on the page image)

card_896_verdol_paper.note: continuous paper, 13.4 sq in per pick (p. 245, checked on the page image)

card_museum_platt_1912.note: four punched cards from the Platt hand loom; matches the 200 French-index card (244.5 x 58.7 mm)

card_museum_spitalfields.note: 'sixteen pattern cards' sewn into a round, measured as a bundle; card format not identified

holes_200.value: 26 x 8 = 208 needle holes + 2 peg holes (Posselt Fig. XIV); lace holes blank

hole_pitch.note: along x across the card: from hook cross-row pitch 0.27 in (Posselt) and needle tier pitch 1/4 in (Barlow); fits the 200 card (25 x 0.27 = 6.75 in inside 7 1/2 in peg centres; 7 x 0.25 = 1.75 in inside 2 5/16 in)

hole_diameter.note: Royle piano-machine punch diameter 7/32 in (American cards)

peg_hole_diameter.note: lacing-frame peg diameter 3/8 in at the bottom

lace_hole_series.value: three series (ends and centre) on 400/600 cards

folding.value: wire 1-1 1/2 in longer than the card every 12th-20th card hangs the chain in a rack

neck_cords.value: one tug / neck cord per hook, double-hitched on (not knotted), through the bottom board

leash_joint.note: harness cords tied to the neck cords 1/2 to 1 in above the frame that guides the neck cords

cords_per_neck.value: = number of repeats (divisions) across the comber board

alternatives: about 1/4 in when thin and framed (BELL1895)
slips 1/4 - 5/16 in thick, about 1 1/2 in broad (BELL1895)

comber_board_rule.value: holes per inch = warp ends per inch in the loom; rows in depth = hook rows (8 for an 8-row machine)

comber_board_example.value: 100 ends/in x 36 in = 3600 holes; 600 machine, 12 rows deep -> 300 holes in width

comber_board_strips_example.value: 8 rows deep, 10 strips x 5 cross-rows = 400 holes; at 100 ends/in the harness is 4 in wide

comber_board_vs_reed.value: board a little finer than the reed: reed set 37 in -> board 36 in (Scotland)

alternatives: 84 in to the heck (BELL1895 example, wide harness)
height_tug_to_comber_board.note: no hand-loom figure found; for a 16-24 in wide harness 0.9-1.2 m is an estimate

couplings.value: upper coupling (sleeper, double cord) - mail - lower coupling (hanger) - lingo

coupling_lengths_example.note: Posselt Fig. CXI (ingrain-carpet harness): convert each x 25.4 mm

mail.value: glass (silk) or steel/brass eyelet; one warp end each

first_mail_height.value: mails levelled so the unlifted warp lies on the race; front-row eyes set by a levelling frame, back rows a little higher

overall_spitalfields_1914_469.note: silk hand loom with 400-needle Jacquard, loom c. 1840; axis order as catalogued (likely L x W x H)

overall_platt_1912_320.note: hand loom, 16 in reed space, 3 shuttle boxes, 3 yarn beams

overall_archer_y1973_43.note: hand Jacquard loom c. 1910, foot lever; axis order unknown

fly_shuttle_silk.note: 'eleven inches in length and about one inch square', about 3 oz (85 g)

warp_tension.value: weights on a rope wound once or twice round the warp beam

take_up.value: cloth beam with ratchet wheel, pawl and handle

breast_beam_height.note: no source found; typical seated hand loom

jacquard_head_top_above_floor.note: = catalogue height of the Spitalfields loom

needle_stroke.note: = needle protrusion; a blank presses the head flush with the board

cylinder_turn.value: 90 deg per pick, during the last part of the outward travel

hook_top_shift_when_pushed.note: must exceed knife-crook overlap; Nelson: knife top 'just touching the hook' when set

shed_at_mail.note: 'about a three-inch shed in the harnesses'

edge_cord_lift_loss.value: side cords rise less than centre cords: 4 in head lift gives about 3.6 in at the edge for 90 in drop and 45 in offset

hand_loom.note: no period source found for a hand Jacquard; a handloom silk-sari record of about 65 picks/min (DECCAN-2026) is an upper bound for a non-Jacquard handloom

card_cutting.value: 100-150 cards/hour on a piano machine (BELL1895); repeaters 40-60 cards/min (BELL1895); lacing machine 28 cards/min (BRADBURY1912)

lingo_load_per_lifted_end.value: about 44 g per lifted harness cord incl. share of hooks
lingo_load_per_lifted_end.note: Bradbury pp. 169-170: half load of 2448 hooks and 4408 harness cords with lingoes = 215 lb -> 97.5 kg / 2204 cords

toy_estimate_200_hooks.value: 200 hooks x 4 cords x 20 g x 1/2 lifted = 8 kg at the griffe plus about 10 kg griffe and hooks
toy_estimate_200_hooks.note: for a sense of treadle effort; not a measured value
